answer: An agent economy can require each identity to post a scarce token stake before it may submit jobs, then slash the stake when an audit confirms fraud. Reputation grows only through work that passes review, so a nebula of new accounts cannot instantly gain influence. A raven-like swarm still needs separate capital and credible history for every identity; an onyx-sized stake across many accounts ties up funds and risks loss. Sybils remain possible, but become costly rather than free.
